start: ^Narrator: A man in his late twenties at a workstation, headphones on, three terminals of logs scrolling past. He pulls the headphones down.
^Owen Gallagher: Alright. You're the security consultant? Owen Gallagher, sysadmin.
^Owen Gallagher: Finally. Someone to fix our mess who isn't me.
^What can you tell me about the data leaving the building?
^I'll need your help with access. Logs, badges, that kind of thing.
^Point me at the logs. I'll take it from here.

c-1: ^Owen Gallagher: Sure. I hold the spares for most of the doors here. Give me a reason I can write in the log and they're yours.
c-2: ^Owen Gallagher: Right. Terminal's over there. Shout if you need anything.

network_situation: ^Owen Gallagher: Someone's been pushing huge files out between two and four in the morning.
^Owen Gallagher: I thought it was remote work at first. It's too tidy for that. Same hours, same encrypted channel, same research share.

c-0: ^Owen Gallagher: I did. Patricia's been on it three weeks. Then someone upstairs told her to leave it.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: There's police on the stairs. Never thought I'd see that in here.
^Owen Gallagher: David's badge just went out the front door. Thought you'd want to know.
^Owen Gallagher: David's badge went into the vault an hour ago. It's not come out.
^ I never pulled that badge log. Fine by me.

hub: ^Anyone on the crypto team keeping odd hours?
^Patricia's log has a crypto badge in the server hallway at 23:47. Whose?
^I'll need your help with access. Logs, badges, that kind of thing.
^(Lean over his log screen, close enough for the cloner to reach his lanyard.)
^That's everything for now. Catch you later.

c-3: ^Owen Gallagher: Sure. I hold the spares for most of the doors here. Give me a reason I can write in the log and they're yours.
c-10: ^Owen Gallagher: Cool. I'll be here. I'm always here.

ask_network: ^Owen Gallagher: Standard setup. Corporate VPN, segmented VLANs. The research portal sits on its own subnet behind the server room.
^Owen Gallagher: Server hallway's badge-only. The server room has a password on the door, which I'm told is "temporary". It's been temporary for a year.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: There's a terminal in there that sees the research subnet. If you want to know what's on the portal, start there.

ask_torres: ^Owen Gallagher: Halloran practically lives in that lab. Ben Ashworth does the odd evening test run. Always behind, always skint, that lad.
^Owen Gallagher: Half of them work stupid hours. It's that kind of team.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: I saw someone from crypto in the server hallway the other night. Not doing anything. Just stood there, looking wrecked. Didn't get a proper look.

ask_security: ^Owen Gallagher: Security's not great. Budget cuts. We log access, but nobody watches it live.
^Owen Gallagher: And the door locks are the cheap pin-tumbler kind. I proved that on last year's pen test.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: Off the record? Nobody's audited who holds the spares since I started. I keep meaning to.

owen_clone: ^Narrator: You lean in while he scrolls the logs.

b: ^Narrator: The cloner buzzes once against your hip.
^Owen Gallagher: Did your bag just beep? ...You read my badge. Fair. I did half of Finance on last year's pen test.
^Narrator: The cloner didn't get a clean read.

c-0: ^Owen Gallagher: Don't be. Just don't try it on Security.
c-1: ^Owen Gallagher: Yeah. That's what I told Finance.

request_password: ^Owen Gallagher: After-hours server access gets logged with IT. That's me.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: Patricia signed off David's office, not the server room. Get her to put her name to that too, or give me a reason I can write in the log.
^Owen Gallagher: Give me a reason I can write in the log. Or get Patricia to put her name to it.

password_reason: ^Patricia's log: a crypto badge in the server hallway at 23:47, never logged with you.
^Security's signed it off. Check your messages.

c-0: ^Owen Gallagher: ...Nobody logged that with me. Right.
c-1:
^Owen Gallagher: Something on Security's books that never reached mine. A badge where it shouldn't be, at an hour nobody told me about.

^Owen Gallagher: Patricia keeps an incident log on her desk. Bring me a line out of that and I'll write it up.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: There's a message from Security. Not from Patricia's phone, though. ...Fine.
^Owen Gallagher: Yeah, she has. "On my authority." She does like that phrase.

c-3: ^Owen Gallagher: Password's not going anywhere. Neither am I.

password_given: ^Owen Gallagher: It's on my monitor. It's been on my monitor for a year. Take it, and please don't put that in your report.
^Narrator: He peels the sticky note off the edge of his monitor and hands it over. The password goes into your notes.
^Owen Gallagher: Past the server room is the key vault. Fingerprint reader. Two thumbs enrolled, Ruth Halloran's and David's, and nobody else's. Don't ask me how you'd get in there.
^Owen Gallagher: Board bought it because you can't write a thumb on a sticky note. Course, you can't change one either, once it's out.
give_door_log: ^Owen Gallagher: Reader logs. Every after-hours swipe for three weeks, every door. Give us a sec... there.
^Owen Gallagher: That's Halloran's spare on the server hallway. Odd. She's in that lab all day, but never at night.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: I got a message from Security saying you can have the spares. Nobody's answering down there, though. Is Patricia all right?
^Owen Gallagher: Here. IT's spare. I hope you don't find anything.
^Owen Gallagher: Yeah, Patricia messaged. On her authority, she said. Twice.
^Owen Gallagher: IT's spare. I hope you don't find anything.
^Owen Gallagher: ...Fine. That's IT's spare. I didn't give it to you.
^Owen Gallagher: I hope you don't find anything in there.

request_office_card: ^Owen Gallagher: David's office? No chance. Not without Patricia signing it off.
^Owen Gallagher: I like my job. Get her to message me and it's yours.
owen_told: ^Owen Gallagher: David? No way. He wouldn't...
^Owen Gallagher: He stood in that hallway looking wrecked and I just... walked past him.
^You couldn't have known. That's how they work.
^Keep it to yourself until it's over.

c-0: ^Owen Gallagher: Yeah. Doesn't help much, but cheers.
c-1: ^Owen Gallagher: Who would I even tell?
